title: Etale base neighbourhood from a field or DVR stalk
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $B$ a commutative $R$-algebra finite and torsion free as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; torsion free means $rb=0$, $0\ne r\in R$, implies $b=0$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal, let $R_{\mathfrak p}$ be localization at that prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and assume $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is either a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ and $F=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Suppose either (i) $\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], or (ii) $F$ is a finite product of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (separable means minimal polynomials have distinct roots). Then there is $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $R[1/f]\to B[1/f]$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], $B$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module, since $R$ is Noetherian and $B$ is finite. Step 1 supplies precisely the free localization required by [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-free-at-prime-spreads]. Apply it to obtain $g\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $B_g$ is finite free over $R_g$. Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R_g$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B_g$, and let $h:X\to Y$ be induced by the structure map.

The ring $R_g$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. A finite $R_g$-module generating set of $B_g$ also generates it as an algebra: its $R_g$-linear combinations already include every element. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $B_g$ a finitely presented $R_g$-algebra, so $h$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its finite free underlying module is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. Apply [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion] with $M=B_g$ to obtain flatness of each stalk over its base stalk; hence $h$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is finite by the affine finite-algebra criterion of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

Let $y=\mathfrak pR_g\in Y$. Its residue field is $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: inverting $g\notin\mathfrak p$ and then all nonzero classes in $R/\mathfrak p$ gives the same fraction field. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $X_y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_g\otimes_{R_g}k)=\operatorname{Spec}F$. The tensor identification sends $(b/g^n)\otimes c$ to $b\otimes g^{-n}c$, with inverse $b\otimes c\mapsto(b/1)\otimes c$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_N$ generate $B$ over $R$, then $b_i\otimes1$ span $F$ over $k$, so $F$ is a finite $k$-algebra. Under either hypothesis (i) or (ii), [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion] therefore gives that $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and hence $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is etale.

source.place: Schemes Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Algebra Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field; Morphisms Tag 02GU (2),(5)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-etale-neighbourhoods] to $h$ and $y$. Step 3 checks flatness and local finite presentation, and Step 4 checks the etale scheme-theoretic fibre. For every point $x\in h^{-1}(y)$ it yields an open neighbourhood $V_x\subseteq X$ such that $V_x\to Y$ is etale. Put $U=\bigcup_{x\in h^{-1}(y)}V_x$. This is open and contains the entire fibre, including when the fibre is empty (then $U=\varnothing$).

The complement $Z=X\setminus U$ is closed. Since $h$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] implies that $h(Z)$ is closed in $Y$. It misses $y$ because $U$ contains all points over $y$. Thus $W=Y\setminus h(Z)$ is an open neighbourhood of $y$ and $h^{-1}(W)\subseteq U$. Regard $Y=D(g)$ as an open of $\operatorname{Spec}R$; the same $W$ is open there and contains $\mathfrak p$. Write its closed complement as $V(I)$. Since $\mathfrak p\notin V(I)$, choose $f\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$, giving $D(f)\subseteq W\subseteq D(g)$. Every point of $h^{-1}(D(f))$ lies in a $V_x$; intersecting with this open retains its etale local presentations. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] the restriction to $h^{-1}(D(f))\to D(f)$ is etale. The principal-open rings are $R_f$ and $B_f$: the preimage is defined by the image of $f$, and since $D(f)\subseteq D(g)$, inverting $f$ already makes $g$ a unit (otherwise a maximal ideal of $R_f$ containing $g$ would give a prime in $D(f)\setminus D(g)$). Therefore this restriction is the required map $R[1/f]\to B[1/f]$.

It is true; I tested B=0 (empty fibre, conclusion vacuous), B=R^n, the generic point, a ramified DVR algebra (excluded), R/(t) (excluded by torsion-freeness) and an inseparable residue extension (excluded). Step 1: the localization criterion plus the DVR freeness lemma (0AUW(3), more-algebra.tex:4954) give B_p finite free. Step 2: 00FP finite presentation plus 0GWM freeness at one prime give g with B_g finite free. Step 3: lfp, flat (via the 00HT(6) tool) and finite (via the 01PB clause of the finite-morphism definition). Step 4: κ(pR_g)=κ(p) and the fibre ring is the actual tensor product ≅ F. The finite-étale algebra criterion covers both (i) and (ii), and its notion of étale is def-weil-etale-morphism (checked in the conventions node; 00U3 at algebra.tex:39394). Step 5: the flat-fibre étale-neighbourhood tool (02GU (1)⇔(2), morphisms.tex:8318) is used only through its statement, and empty fibres are allowed. Step 6: a finite map is closed, f∈I∖p gives D(f)⊆W⊆D(g), and h⁻¹(D(f))=Spec B_f because g is a unit in R_f. No duplicates: the codim-one étale-neighbourhood and trace-discriminant nodes state different things. I accept the two tool_uses (00HT localization and the flat-fibre étale criterion).
